summary:
Red Base: Junior Commander is a playful, blocky Roblox game for kids aged 7–12, created in response to the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge. The player becomes a young base commander on Mars. They set up solar panels, water drills, oxygen generators and greenhouses, connect them with corridors, and make sure the colony never runs out of power, water, oxygen or food.

The game teaches through action. Step-by-step quests explain where astronauts get their water and air. Event cards give kids simple choices with real consequences. Sandstorms show up on the minimap before they hit, which teaches kids to plan ahead and respond to danger. Our facts about Mars are based on NASA data.

We want kids to explore space where they already spend their time: on Roblox. Instead of reading about a mission, they can live it. They can make mistakes, try again, and learn that an astronaut’s job is about teamwork, logic and looking after resources. Along the way, they practice cause-and-effect thinking and responsibility.
details:
Red Base: Junior Commander is a Roblox game in which a child aged 7–12 becomes the commander of a base on Mars. They start with a small module and then build more structures:

  • a solar panel provides power;
  • a drill extracts water from underground ice;
  • a generator produces oxygen;
  • a greenhouse provides food;
  • a mine provides ore;
  • a warehouse increases storage capacity;
  • a launch pad lets you send off a rocket.

Players connect the buildings with corridors and cables. When a building needs something or has something to collect, a speech bubble with an icon appears above it. Players can walk into some buildings, such as the greenhouse, as their astronaut.

The game is guided by 14 step-by-step quests, each with a simple hint and a reward. In the shop, players can trade resources for coins. Every few minutes a sandstorm rolls in. The game warns players ahead of time, and the minimap shows where the dust cloud is coming from. The minimap also shows the player’s buildings, including the ones that need help.

Benefits and Goals

Kids learn what life on a Mars base is really like:

  • energy, water, oxygen and food have to stay in balance;
  • resources need to be planned;
  • hazards such as dust storms have to be handled ahead of time.

The game teaches cause-and-effect thinking without long texts, through action and short messages. We want to reach kids where they already spend their time, on Roblox, and spark their curiosity about space and STEM.

Tools

  • Roblox Studio and the Luau language: mechanics, interface and buildings.
  • Python with the Pillow library: some of the interface icons.
  • Google Slides: the presentation.
  • Our facts about Mars, such as water ice, dust storms and surface conditions, are based on the NASA materials listed in the NASA Data field.
  • We used AI tools: an AI assistant helped with the code and the interface design, and the concept art was made with an image generator and is labeled as AI-generated.

What Makes It Creative

  • A playful, blocky style instead of a dry simulation.
  • An interface in the style of popular Roblox games: big icons, colorful building cards and a quest progress bar.
  • A radar minimap that shows the incoming storm.
  • Custom building icons.
  • Mars isn’t just a backdrop here. It’s an “opponent” you have to understand in order to survive.

What We Focused On

  • Player age: little text, big buttons, clear icons and no violence.
  • The game runs on both computers and phones, because the interface adapts to the screen automatically.
  • Safety: the game doesn’t collect any personal data, and our materials don’t show team members’ faces or names.
  • Performance: we reworked the interface so it runs smoothly on lower-end devices too.

What’s Next

Our concept also includes:

  • event cards with choices and consequences;
  • lessons with a robot helper;
  • an upgrade tree and a colony progress bar;
  • more NASA mission data, for example from the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers.
